response: The fundamental bottleneck in local AI inference and training has long been the memory capacity of the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). In a conventional discrete GPU architecture, the processor (the GPU die) and its memory (High Bandwidth Memory, or HBM) are physically separate components connected via a high-speed bus, such as PCIe or NVLink. This separation creates a distinct "memory wall." When a Large Language Model (LLM) or a diffusion model exceeds the capacity of the GPU's VRAM, the system must offload layers to the system RAM (CPU memory).
